note: Metre is taught, not drilled: the skill's only kind is `recognise`, and there is nothing to parse or fill in. So this file holds four illustrative lines of our own verse rather than the twelve practice sentences a drillable skill gets, and each carries its scansion in `scan`. Every word is inside the cumulative vocabulary to chapter 34 or a name of the book's cast; because the lines are ours and not the poets', a learner may be shown a whole line scanned without quoting anyone.

sentences.la: Pulchra puella sedet, spectat rīdetque poētam.
sentences.en: A pretty girl sits, watches the poet and laughs at him.
sentences.scan: Pulchra pu | ella se | det, spec | tat rī | detque po | ētam  —  – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – – | – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | – –
sentences.note: An illustrative hexameter of our own, not a practice sentence. The foot boundary falls inside puella, which is the point of the first step: feet are counted in syllables, not in words.

sentences.la: Ille tamen tacitus stat, mala verba timet.
sentences.en: He, though, stands silent and fears unkind words.
sentences.scan: Ille ta | men taci | tus || stat mala | verba ti | met  —  – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | – || – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ ⏑ | –
sentences.note: An illustrative pentameter of our own, not a practice sentence. It follows ec-01, so the two together make one elegiac couplet. stat is the syllable that opens the second half, straight after the break.

sentences.la: Nōn omnēs nautae sunt fortēs, nec bona nāvis.
sentences.en: Not all sailors are brave, and the ship is no good one either.
sentences.scan: Nōn om | nēs nau | tae sunt | fortēs | nec bona | nāvis  —  – – | – – | – – | – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | – –
sentences.note: An illustrative hexameter of our own, not a practice sentence. Four spondees in a row, then the fifth-foot dactyl the hexameter almost always keeps.

sentences.en: You are willing to trust nobody, Marcus my friend.
sentences.scan: Nūllī | crēdere | vīs a | mīce | Mārce  —  – – | – ⏑ ⏑ | – ⏑ | – ⏑ | – ⏓   (eleven syllables)
sentences.note: An illustrative hendecasyllable of our own, not a practice sentence. crēdere fills the second foot exactly, the one dactyl the line has.
